title: Nifty rebounds past 22,490 as IT, Consumption stocks lead rally - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
The Nifty’s advance-decline ratio stood at 46:4, reflecting the breadth of the recovery.

Benchmarks staged a broad recovery by midday on Friday, reversing most of Thursday’s losses as short-covering in banking and IT stocks drove the advance. The Sensex climbed 806.08 points or 1.13 per cent to 72,399.32 at 13.05 pm, from its previous close of 71,593.24 and an opening of 71,776.67. The Nifty 50 rose 261.35 points or 1.18 per cent to 22,493.15, recovering from a previous close of 22,231.80 and an open of 22,314.95.

The Nifty’s advance-decline ratio stood at 46:4, reflecting the breadth of the recovery. On BSE, 2,195 stocks advanced against 1,955 declining, while 238 remained unchanged. Ninety-two stocks hit 52-week highs against 225 at 52-week lows, signalling that weakness in the broader market persists below the headline recovery.

ITC led Nifty gainers, rising 4.33 per cent to ₹266.05. TCS advanced 3.71 per cent to ₹2,153.00 after reporting a 14.9 per cent year-on-year rise in net profit to ₹13,884 crore for the July–September quarter, with annualised AI-related revenue reaching $3.1 billion, crossing 10 per cent of total revenue. Eicher Motors rose 3.60 per cent to ₹7,011.00, Apollo Hospitals climbed 3.52 per cent to ₹7,936.00, and Adani Ports gained 3.14 per cent to ₹1,761.60.

TCS shares surge 4% post-results; analysts split on outlook

The Nifty IT index was the best-performing sectoral index, while Nifty Oil & Gas was the sole sectoral laggard. “The frontline indices witnessed a sharp rebound on the back of short covering in frontline banking and IT stocks, with HDFC Bank, TCS and Infosys being the top three contributors in Nifty,” SBI Securities said in its mid-market update.

On the losing side, BSE fell 2.00 per cent to ₹3,268.00, Reliance Industries slipped 0.45 per cent to ₹1,172.70, and JSW Steel edged down 0.15 per cent to ₹1,173.40.

In commodities, precious metals gained ground as the dollar softened and US Treasury yields eased. COMEX Gold rose 1.03 per cent to $4,200 per ounce and COMEX Silver climbed 1.59 per cent to $60.37. Domestically, MCX Gold opened with a gap-up at ₹150,851, up 0.81 per cent, while MCX Silver rose around 1.2 per cent to ₹224,096. Crude oil gave back some of Thursday’s sharp gains, with WTI trading below $91 per barrel, down 0.79 per cent, and Brent near $103, down about 0.7 per cent. MCX Crude fell 1.20 per cent to ₹8,760. The rupee held near ₹96.75 to the dollar, marginally off its recent record low of ₹96.85, with the currency remaining under pressure from sustained foreign outflows and high oil prices.

The rebound came despite persistent macro headwinds. Foreign portfolio investors have extended their selling to ten consecutive sessions, offloading ₹36,210 crore worth of equities through the exchanges in October so far. The RBI’s 25-basis-point rate hike to 5.50 per cent and elevated US yields near 5.22 per cent continue to raise the cost of holding emerging-market assets.

IT stocks rallied even as the sector faces fresh regulatory pressure from Washington’s suspension of TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCL Technologies, Cognizant and Capgemini from the PERM green-card programme. Analysts noted the immediate operational impact is limited since existing H-1B employment is unaffected, but warned of higher localisation and compliance costs ahead.

Technically, SBI Securities placed Nifty support at 22,330–22,350 and resistance at 22,640–22,660, with an extension toward 22,810 possible on a breakout. Sensex support was identified at 71,900, with resistance at 72,800. Options data showed meaningful call writing at the 22,500 and 22,600 strikes, with significant put open interest at 22,400 and 22,300, indicating the market remains in a “wait-and-watch” mode despite the day’s gains.
